title: Unit 4: Quadratic Equations and Complex Numbers

teach.title: Reading vertex form
text: Vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k.
The vertex is (h, k). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line x = h.
If a > 0 the parabola opens up and the vertex is a minimum. If a < 0 it opens down and the vertex is a maximum.

steps: h = 3 and k = 5, so the vertex is (3, 5).
a = −2 < 0, so it opens down. The maximum value is 5.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = (x − 4)² + 7?
questions.hint: In (x − h), the vertex uses h. Watch the sign.
questions.solution: The form is (x − h), so x − 4 gives h = 4. k = 7. Vertex: (4, 7).

questions.prompt: The axis of symmetry of y = (x − 6)² − 2 is x = h. What is h?
questions.hint: The axis passes through the vertex.
questions.solution: x − 6 means h = 6. The axis is x = 6.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = −3(x + 2)² + 1?
What is the minimum value of y = 2(x − 5)² + 9?
questions.hint: a is positive, so the vertex is the lowest point. Its y-value is k.
questions.solution: a = 2 > 0, so the parabola opens up. The minimum is k = 9.

questions.prompt: Which describes y = −½(x − 1)² + 4?
questions.hint: Look at the sign of a only.
questions.solution: a = −½ < 0. The parabola opens down, so the vertex is a maximum.

questions.prompt: The vertex of y = (x + 3)² − 8 has x-coordinate h. What is h?
Which parabola has vertex (−1, 6) and opens up?
questions.hint: Check the sign of h, the sign of k, and the sign of a.
questions.solution: h = −1 gives (x + 1). k = 6 is added. Opening up needs a > 0. So y = 2(x + 1)² + 6.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum value of y = −4(x − 2)² + 11?
questions.hint: a is negative, so the vertex is the highest point.
questions.solution: a = −4 < 0, so it opens down. The maximum is k = 11.

teach.title: Transformations of y = x²
text: In y = a(x − h)² + k, h slides the graph right (positive h) or left (negative h). k slides it up or down.
If |a| > 1 the graph is narrower. If 0 < |a| < 1 it is wider. If a < 0 it is flipped upside down.

example.problem: Describe y = −½(x + 4)² − 3 compared to y = x²
steps: a = −½: reflect over the x-axis, and the graph is wider because ½ < 1.

questions.prompt: How does y = (x − 5)² compare to y = x²?
questions.hint: A number inside the parentheses moves the graph sideways.
questions.solution: x − 5 shifts the graph right 5 units.

questions.prompt: How does y = x² − 6 compare to y = x²?
questions.hint: A number added outside moves the graph up or down.

questions.prompt: Which parabola is the narrowest?
questions.hint: Compare the size of |a|. Bigger |a| is narrower.
questions.solution: |a| is 2, 0.5, 1, and 0.25. The largest is 2, so y = 2x² is narrowest.

questions.prompt: Describe y = −(x + 2)² + 1 compared to y = x².
questions.hint: a = −1 flips it. x + 2 and + 1 shift it.
questions.solution: a = −1: reflect over the x-axis. x + 2: left 2. + 1: up 1.

questions.prompt: Which equation is y = x² shifted right 3 and up 4?
questions.hint: Right 3 goes inside as x − 3. Up 4 goes outside as + 4.

questions.prompt: The parabola y = a(x − 1)² + 2 passes through (2, 5). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 2 and y = 5, then solve for a.

questions.prompt: A parabola has vertex (3, −1) and passes through (5, 7). Its equation is y = a(x − 3)² − 1. What is a?
questions.hint: Put x = 5 and y = 7 into the equation.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of the graph?
questions.hint: Read the x-coordinate of the top point first.
questions.solution: The highest point is at x = 2 and y = 3. Vertex: (2, 3).

teach.title: Writing an equation from a graph
text: Read the vertex (h, k) off the graph and put it in y = a(x − h)² + k.
Then pick one other point on the graph, substitute it, and solve for a.

example.problem: A parabola has vertex (1, −2) and passes through (3, 2). Write its equation.

questions.prompt: Read the graph. What is its vertex?
questions.hint: The graph opens up, so the vertex is the lowest point.
questions.solution: The lowest point is at x = −2, y = −3. Vertex: (−2, −3).

questions.prompt: The graph shows a parabola. Its axis of symmetry is x = h. What is h?
questions.hint: The axis goes straight through the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (1, 4), so the axis is x = 1.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum value of the graphed function?
questions.hint: The maximum is the y-value of the top point.
questions.solution: The top point is (3, 5). The maximum value is 5.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches the graph? Check the point (3, −2).
questions.hint: The vertex is (1, −4). Then test the point (3, −2) in each choice.
questions.solution: Vertex (1, −4) gives (x − 1)² − 4. At x = 3: a(2)² − 4 = −2, so 4a = 2 and a = ½. y = ½(x − 1)² − 4.

questions.prompt: A parabola has vertex (−1, −3) and passes through (1, 5). Its equation is y = a(x + 1)² − 3. What is a?
Which equation has vertex (4, −1) and passes through (6, −5)?
questions.hint: Find a from the point: substitute x = 6, y = −5 into y = a(x − 4)² − 1.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = −(x + 3)² + 8?
questions.hint: The y-intercept is the value of y when x = 0.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = 2(x − 1)² − 5?

teach.title: Putting it together
text: Vertex form gives the vertex, axis, direction, and max or min at a glance.
To find x-intercepts, set y = 0, isolate (x − h)², and take square roots.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about y = 3(x − 2)² − 7?
choices: Opens up, minimum value −7 at x = 2
Opens up, minimum value 2 at x = −7
Opens down, maximum value −7 at x = 2
Opens up, minimum value −7 at x = −2
questions.hint: Find the vertex, then look at the sign of a.
questions.solution: Vertex (2, −7). a = 3 > 0, so it opens up and the minimum is −7 at x = 2.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = 5(x + 4)² + 13?
questions.hint: The minimum is the y-value of the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−4, 13) and a > 0. The minimum value is 13.

questions.prompt: The function y = −(x − 3)² + k has a maximum value of 6. What is k?
questions.hint: The maximum of this form is k.
questions.solution: The vertex is (3, k) and the maximum is k. So k = 6.

questions.prompt: Which function has the greatest maximum value?
questions.hint: Only parabolas that open down have a maximum. Compare their k values.
questions.solution: The last one opens up, so it has no maximum. The maxima of the others are 3, 5, and 4. The greatest is 5.

questions.prompt: A parabola has vertex (2, 3) and passes through (4, −5). Its equation is y = a(x − 2)² + 3. What is a?
Find the x-intercepts of y = −2(x − 3)² + 8. Give both values.
y = 3(x − 2)² + k passes through (4, 10). What is k?
Which equation has vertex (−2, 5) and opens down?
questions.hint: Opens down means a < 0. Then fix the signs for h and k.
questions.solution: h = −2 gives (x + 2). k = 5. Opening down needs a < 0. So y = −3(x + 2)² + 5.

teach.title: Axis and vertex from standard form
text: Standard form is y = ax² + bx + c. The y-intercept is c.
The axis of symmetry is x = −b / (2a).
The vertex is on the axis. Put the axis value into the equation to find its y-coordinate.

questions.prompt: The axis of symmetry of y = x² + 6x + 1 is x = ? Type the number.
The axis of symmetry of y = x² − 10x + 4 is x = ? Type the number.
The axis of symmetry of y = 2x² + 8x − 1 is x = ? Type the number.
What is the axis of symmetry of y = −x² + 4x + 3?
questions.hint: a is negative here. Keep the signs when you use −b / (2a).

questions.prompt: The vertex of y = 3x² − 12x + 5 is (2, k). What is k?
What is the vertex of y = x² − 4x + 1?
questions.hint: Find the axis first, then the y-value.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = x² + 2x − 8? Type the y-value.
What is the y-intercept (as a point) of y = −2x² + 5x + 9?
questions.hint: Put x = 0 in. Only c is left.
questions.solution: At x = 0, y = 9. The point is (0, 9).

teach.title: Maximum, minimum, domain, and range
text: If a > 0 the vertex is the minimum. If a < 0 it is the maximum.
The domain of every quadratic is all real numbers.
The range depends on the vertex y-value k: y ≥ k if it opens up, y ≤ k if it opens down.

steps: a < 0, so it opens down: range y ≤ 4.

questions.prompt: Does y = −3x² + 6x + 1 have a maximum or a minimum?
questions.hint: Only the sign of a decides the direction.
questions.solution: a = −3 < 0, so it opens down and the vertex is a maximum.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = x² − 6x + 11?
questions.hint: Axis first: x = −b / (2a). Then find y there.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum value of y = −x² + 8x − 3?
What is the domain of y = 2x² + 3x − 5?
questions.hint: Can you put any x into a quadratic?
questions.solution: You can substitute any real number for x. The domain is all real numbers.

questions.prompt: What is the range of y = x² − 4x + 7?
questions.hint: Find the vertex y-value. Then check which way it opens.
questions.solution: Axis x = 2. y = 4 − 8 + 7 = 3. a > 0, so the range is y ≥ 3.

questions.prompt: What is the range of y = −2x² + 12x − 5?
questions.solution: Axis x = 3. y = −18 + 36 − 5 = 13. a < 0, so the range is y ≤ 13.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = 2x² − 12x + 20?
What is the maximum value of y = −x² − 6x − 2?

teach.title: Working backward
text: The axis formula is an equation. If you know the axis, you can solve for a missing a or b.
Parabolas are symmetric: two points with the same y-value are the same distance from the axis.

example.problem: y = x² + bx + 1 has axis x = 3. Find b.

questions.prompt: y = x² + bx + 5 has axis x = 2. What is b?
y = 2x² + bx − 3 has axis x = 3. What is b?
y = −x² + bx has axis x = 5. What is b?
y = ax² − 12x + 1 has axis x = 3. What is a?
Which parabola has axis of symmetry x = 1?
questions.solution: The axes are 1, −1, ½, and ½. Only y = x² − 2x + 5 has x = 1.

questions.prompt: y = x² − 8x + c has a minimum value of 3. What is c?
questions.hint: The minimum is at the axis x = 4.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = −2x² + 4x + 1?
y = x² − 6x + 4 has y-intercept (0, 4). Another point with y = 4 is (n, 4). What is n?
questions.hint: The axis is x = 3. The point (0, 4) is 3 units from it.
questions.solution: Axis x = 3. (0, 4) is 3 left of the axis, so the mirror point is 3 right: x = 6.

teach.title: Full problems
text: Use the axis to find the vertex. Then compare vertices to compare parabolas.
To find x-intercepts, set y = 0 and solve.

example.problem: Find the minimum value of y = x² + 4x + 9

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about y = 3x² − 6x + 2?
questions.hint: Axis, then y-value, then the sign of a.
questions.solution: Axis x = 6 / 6 = 1. y = 3 − 6 + 2 = −1. a > 0, so it is a minimum.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = ½x² − 2x + 5?
What is the range of y = −x² + 2x + 8?
questions.hint: It opens down. Find the vertex y-value.
questions.solution: Axis x = 1. y = −1 + 2 + 8 = 9. It opens down, so y ≤ 9.

questions.prompt: y = x² + 4x + k has a minimum value of −1. What is k?
y = −3x² + bx + 2 has axis x = 2. What is b?
Which function has the lowest minimum value?
questions.hint: Find the vertex y-value of each.
questions.solution: The minima are 2, 2, 1, and 3. The lowest is 1, from y = x² + 4x + 5.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = x² − 6x + 5. Give both values.
What is the minimum value of y = 2x² − 8x + 6?

teach.title: GCF and trinomials with a = 1
text: Always pull out the greatest common factor first.
To factor x² + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. Then write (x + m)(x + n).

steps: Two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7: 3 and 4.

teach.title: GCF example
text: The GCF is the biggest number and the highest power of x that divides every term.

steps: GCF of 6 and 9 is 3. Both terms have x.

questions.prompt: Factor 8x² + 12x.
questions.hint: Find the GCF of both the numbers and the x parts. Take out all of it.
questions.solution: GCF of 8 and 12 is 4, and both have x, so the GCF is 4x. 8x² / 4x = 2x and 12x / 4x = 3. Answer: 4x(2x + 3).

questions.prompt: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + m)(x + n). Type m and n.
questions.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7.
questions.solution: 3 · 4 = 12 and 3 + 4 = 7. So m and n are 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: Factor x² + 9x + 20.
questions.hint: Which pair multiplies to 20 and adds to 9?

questions.prompt: Factor x² − 5x + 6.
questions.hint: The middle term is negative and the last term is positive, so both numbers are negative.

questions.prompt: Factor x² + 2x − 15.
questions.hint: The last term is negative, so one number is positive and one is negative. The bigger one is positive.

questions.prompt: x² − x − 12 = (x + m)(x + n). Type m and n (they can be negative).
questions.solution: 3 · (−4) = −12 and 3 + (−4) = −1. So m and n are 3 and −4.

questions.prompt: Factor x² − 10x + 16.
questions.hint: Both numbers are negative. List the pairs that multiply to 16.

questions.prompt: Factor 5x³ − 15x².
questions.hint: Both terms share x², not just x.

teach.title: Trinomials with a ≠ 1
text: Multiply a · c. Find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b.
Use them to split the middle term, then factor by grouping.

steps: a · c = 6. Numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 7: 1 and 6.

questions.prompt: Factor 2x² + 5x + 2.
questions.hint: ac = 4. Which two numbers multiply to 4 and add to 5?

questions.prompt: To factor 3x² + 10x + 8, find two numbers that multiply to ac = 24 and add to 10. Type both.
questions.hint: List the pairs that multiply to 24.

questions.prompt: Factor 3x² + 11x + 6.
questions.hint: ac = 18. Which pair multiplies to 18 and adds to 11?

questions.prompt: Factor 2x² − 7x + 3.
questions.hint: Middle term negative, last term positive: both signs are negative.

questions.prompt: Factor 4x² + 4x − 3.
questions.hint: ac = −12. Find two numbers that multiply to −12 and add to 4.

questions.prompt: Factor 6x² − x − 2.
questions.hint: ac = −12. Find two numbers that multiply to −12 and add to −1.

questions.prompt: To factor 5x² + 13x + 6, find two numbers that multiply to ac = 30 and add to 13. Type both.
questions.hint: List the pairs that multiply to 30.

questions.prompt: Factor completely: 12x² + 10x − 12.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF of 2 first. Then factor 6x² + 5x − 6.

teach.title: Special patterns
text: Difference of squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). A sum of squares like x² + 9 does not factor.
Perfect square trinomials: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² and a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)².

steps: It is a difference of squares.

questions.prompt: Factor x² − 49.
Factor 9x² − 16.
questions.hint: Take the square root of each term first.

questions.prompt: Factor x² + 10x + 25.
questions.hint: Is the first term a square, the last term a square, and the middle twice their product?

questions.prompt: Factor x² − 12x + 36.
Factor 4x² + 12x + 9.
x² + kx + 49 is a perfect square trinomial, and k is positive. What is k?
questions.hint: The middle term is 2 times the square roots of the first and last terms.

questions.prompt: Factor x² + 36.
questions.hint: Is it a difference or a sum of squares? Multiply your guesses to check.
questions.solution: A sum of squares does not factor over the real numbers. (x + 6)(x − 6) = x² − 36, which is not it.

questions.prompt: Factor 2x² − 50.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF first. What is left?

teach.title: Choosing a method
text: Order of steps: GCF first. Then count terms. Two terms: difference of squares? Three terms: trinomial.
Check by multiplying back. Keep factoring until no factor can be broken down more.

questions.prompt: Factor 3x² − 27.
questions.hint: GCF first, then a difference of squares.

questions.prompt: Factor completely: x⁴ − 16.
questions.hint: After the first split, one factor is still a difference of squares.

questions.prompt: Factor 2x² + 12x + 18.
questions.hint: GCF first. The trinomial left is a perfect square.

questions.prompt: Factor 6x² + 7x − 3.
questions.hint: ac = −18. Find two numbers that multiply to −18 and add to 7.

questions.prompt: Factor x³ − 5x² − 14x.
questions.hint: Take out x first. Then factor the trinomial.

questions.prompt: (x + 8)(x − 3) = x² + bx − 24. What is b?
questions.hint: Multiply out and combine the x terms: 8x and −3x.

questions.prompt: Factor x² − 6x − 16.
Factor 20x² − 45.

teach.title: Zero product property
text: If A · B = 0, then A = 0 or B = 0. A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero.
So when an equation is already factored and equals 0, set each factor equal to 0 and solve.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 2)(x + 7) = 0. Give both solutions.
questions.solution: x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2. x + 7 = 0 gives x = −7.

questions.prompt: Solve (x + 4)(x + 1) = 0. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Each factor equals 0 separately. Watch the signs.
questions.solution: x + 4 = 0 gives x = −4. x + 1 = 0 gives x = −1.

questions.prompt: Solve x(x − 9) = 0. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: The factor x is also a factor.
questions.solution: x = 0 or x − 9 = 0. So x = 0 or x = 9.

questions.hint: For 2x − 1 = 0, add 1 and then divide by 2.
questions.solution: 2x − 1 = 0 gives x = ½. x + 6 = 0 gives x = −6.

questions.prompt: Solve (3x + 5)(x − 4) = 0. Give both solutions (use a fraction).
questions.hint: Solve 3x + 5 = 0 by subtracting 5 and then dividing by 3.

questions.prompt: Why can you set each factor equal to 0 in (x − 1)(x + 2) = 0?
choices: The factors must be equal to each other
The sum of the factors must be 0
A product is 0 only when at least one factor is 0
questions.hint: Think about what multiplying by 0 does.
questions.solution: If neither factor is 0, the product cannot be 0. So at least one factor must be 0.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 8)² = 0.
questions.solution: x − 8 = 0, so x = 8. It is a double solution.

questions.prompt: Solve 5x(x + 3)(x − 2) = 0. Give all three solutions.
questions.hint: Each factor with x in it can be 0. The 5 cannot.
questions.solution: 5x = 0 gives x = 0. x + 3 = 0 gives x = −3. x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2.

teach.title: Set it equal to 0 first
text: The zero product property only works when one side is 0.
Move every term to one side, factor, then set each factor to 0.
Never divide both sides by x: you will lose the solution x = 0.

steps: Move everything to one side: x² − 7x + 12 = 0.

questions.prompt: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve x² + 3x − 10 = 0. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Two numbers that multiply to −10 and add to 3.

questions.prompt: Solve x² − 9 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve x² + 8x = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve 2x² − 8x = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve x² = 7x − 12. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Move everything to the left side first.

questions.prompt: Solve x² + 14x + 49 = 0.
Solve x² − 4x = 5.
questions.hint: Do not factor x(x − 4) = 5. Move the 5 first.

teach.title: Harder equations to factor
text: Use all your factoring tools: GCF, a ≠ 1, difference of squares, perfect squares.
A GCF that is just a number never gives a solution. It does not change the answers.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0. Give both solutions (use a fraction).
Solve 3x² − 10x + 8 = 0. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: ac = 24. Find two numbers that multiply to 24 and add to −10.

questions.prompt: Solve 6x² + x − 2 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve 4x² − 25 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve 3x² + 12x + 12 = 0.
Solve 2x² − 18 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve 5x² = 20x. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Do not divide by x. Move 20x to the left.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ − 4x = 0. Give all three solutions.
questions.hint: Factor out x. Then use difference of squares.

teach.title: Word problems
text: Define a variable, write an equation, set it equal to 0, and factor.
Check each answer in the story. A length cannot be negative, so some solutions get thrown out.

example.problem: A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide. Its area is 40 cm². Find the width.
steps: Let w = width. Length is w + 3. w(w + 3) = 40.
w = −8 or w = 5. A width cannot be negative, so w = 5.

questions.prompt: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 56. What is the smaller integer?
questions.hint: Let n and n + 1 be the integers. Write n(n + 1) = 56.
questions.solution: n² + n − 56 = 0, so (n + 8)(n − 7) = 0. n = 7 (n = −8 is not positive). Check: 7 · 8 = 56.

questions.prompt: A number squared equals 4 times the number plus 12. Find both numbers.
questions.hint: Write x² = 4x + 12, then move everything to one side.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide. Its area is 40 cm². What is the width in cm?
questions.hint: Width w, length w + 3. Area = w(w + 3).

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown so that its height is h = −16t² + 48t feet after t seconds. When does it land (t > 0)? Type the number of seconds.
questions.solution: −16t² + 48t = 0, so −16t(t − 3) = 0. t = 0 (the throw) or t = 3. It lands at t = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve (x + 3)(x − 1) = 12. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Do not set each factor equal to 12. Multiply out and move the 12 first.

questions.prompt: What is the right first step to solve x² + x = 20?
choices: Take the square root of both sides
questions.hint: The zero product property needs 0 on one side.
questions.solution: Subtract 20 from both sides to get x² + x − 20 = 0. Then factor.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x² + 7x = 15. Give both solutions (use a fraction).
A square has side length x + 2 cm and area 49 cm². What is x?
questions.hint: Write (x + 2)² = 49, multiply out, and move 49 over.
questions.solution: x² + 4x + 4 = 49, so x² + 4x − 45 = 0. (x + 9)(x − 5) = 0. x = 5 (x = −9 would make a negative side).

teach.title: Solving x² = k
text: If x² = k and k > 0, then x = ±√k: two solutions, one positive and one negative.
If k = 0, then x = 0. If k < 0, there is no real solution, because a real number squared is never negative.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = 49. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Take the square root of both sides. Remember ±.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = 25/4. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Take the root of the top and the bottom.

questions.prompt: Solve x² − 36 = 0. Give both solutions.
Solve x² = 20.
questions.hint: Simplify √20 by pulling out the perfect square 4.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = −36.
questions.hint: Can a real number squared be negative?
questions.solution: A real number squared is never negative. So there is no real solution.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x² = 75. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by 3 before taking the root.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = 18.
Solve 2x² + 1 = 33. Give both solutions.
questions.hint: Subtract 1, divide by 2, then take the root.

teach.title: Simplifying radicals
text: Look for the biggest perfect square factor: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, ...
Use √(a · b) = √a · √b. The square root of the perfect square comes out front.

questions.prompt: What is √49?
Simplify √50.
√48 = k√3. What is k?
Simplify √75.
Simplify √200.
√72 = k√2. What is k?
Simplify 3√28.
√45 = k√5. What is k?

teach.title: Solving (x − h)² = k
text: When a squared expression equals a number, take the square root of both sides: x − h = ±√k.
Then solve for x. If k is not a perfect square, leave the answer as h ± √k.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 3)² = 16. Give both solutions.
questions.solution: x − 3 = 4 gives x = 7. x − 3 = −4 gives x = −1.

questions.prompt: Solve (x + 5)² = 4. Give both solutions.
questions.solution: x + 5 = 2 gives x = −3. x + 5 = −2 gives x = −7.

questions.prompt: Solve (x + 1)² = 25. Give both solutions.
questions.solution: x + 1 = 5 gives x = 4. x + 1 = −5 gives x = −6.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 4)² = −1.
questions.solution: A real square is never −1. No real solution.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 2)² = 7.
questions.hint: 7 is not a perfect square. Leave the root.

questions.prompt: Solve (2x − 1)² = 9. Give both solutions.
Solve (x + 6)² = 12.
Solve 3(x − 1)² = 48. Give both solutions.

teach.title: Mixed and applied
text: Isolate the squared part first, then take ±√. Check the sign of what is left: negative means no real solution.
In a word problem, a length or time must be positive, so throw out a negative answer.

example.problem: An object is dropped. Its height drop is d = 16t². How long to fall 144 feet?
steps: Time cannot be negative, so t = 3 seconds.

questions.prompt: Solve 4x² = 100. Give both solutions.
Solve 2x² + 18 = 0.
questions.hint: Isolate x². What sign does it have?
questions.solution: 2x² = −18, so x² = −36. No real number squared is −36.

questions.prompt: Solve (x − 7)² = 0.
questions.hint: The only number whose square is 0 is 0.

questions.prompt: Solve 2(x + 3)² = 50.
A square has area 81 cm². What is its side length in cm?
questions.hint: Area = side². A side cannot be negative.
questions.solution: s² = 81, so s = ±9. A length is positive, so s = 9.

questions.prompt: A dropped object falls d = 16t² feet in t seconds. How many seconds to fall 144 feet?
questions.solution: t² = 9, so t = ±3. Time cannot be negative, so t = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve 3(x − 1)² = 24.
Solve (x + 4)² − 49 = 0. Give both solutions.
For which value of k does (x − 2)² = k have no real solution?
questions.hint: A real square is never negative.
questions.solution: If k < 0 there is no real solution. Only −4 is negative.

teach.title: The number i
text: No real number squares to a negative. So we define i = √(−1). That gives i² = −1.
For a negative radicand, pull out the −1: √(−n) = i√n.

teach.title: Simplifying √(−n) when n is not a perfect square
text: Pull out i first. Then simplify the radical the usual way, by taking out perfect squares.
Write the i in front of the radical so it is not mistaken for part of the root: 2i√3.

questions.prompt: What is the value of i²?
questions.hint: i is defined as √(−1). Square both sides of that.

questions.prompt: √(−49) = bi. What is b?
Simplify √(−25).
questions.hint: Take out the −1 as i, then take the square root of 25.

questions.prompt: √(−81) = bi. What is b?
questions.hint: Think of what number times itself is 81.

questions.prompt: Simplify √(−20).

questions.hint: Write each term as a multiple of i, then add.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a real number?
questions.hint: A real number can be placed on the number line. Check each one.
questions.solution: −√16 = −4, ∛(−8) = −2 and √0 = 0 are all real. √(−16) = 4i is imaginary.

questions.prompt: √(−18) = 3i√b. What is b?

teach.title: The powers of i repeat
text: i¹ = i, i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1. Then the pattern starts over.
To simplify iⁿ, divide n by 4 and keep the remainder. Remainder 1 gives i, 2 gives −1, 3 gives −i, and 0 gives 1.

questions.prompt: What is i³?
What is i⁴?
Simplify i⁸. Give a number.
Simplify i¹³.
questions.hint: Divide 13 by 4 and use the remainder.

questions.prompt: Simplify i²².
questions.hint: Divide 22 by 4 and use the remainder.

questions.prompt: To simplify i⁴⁷, divide 47 by 4. What is the remainder?
Simplify i⁴⁷.
questions.hint: Use the remainder from dividing 47 by 4.

questions.prompt: Simplify i³⁸ + i⁴¹.
questions.hint: Simplify each power on its own first.
questions.solution: 38 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2, so i³⁸ = −1. 41 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 1, so i⁴¹ = i. The sum is −1 + i.

teach.title: Solving x² = −k
text: Take the square root of both sides, as always. When the number is negative, the answers are imaginary.
x² = −k gives x = ±i√k. There are two solutions, and neither is a real number.

steps: Square root of both sides: x = ±√(−16).

teach.title: Get x² alone first
text: If there is a number added to or multiplying x², undo it before you take the square root.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = −9.
questions.hint: A negative number under the root gives i. There are two solutions.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = −64.
questions.hint: Take the square root of both sides.

questions.prompt: The solutions of x² = −49 are ±bi. What is b?
Solve x² + 25 = 0.
Solve x² + 12 = 0.
Solve 3x² = −75.
How many real solutions does x² = −10 have?
questions.hint: The square of a real number is never negative.
questions.solution: x = ±i√10 are not real numbers. There are 0 real solutions.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x² + 32 = 0.

teach.title: Convert to i before you multiply
text: The rule √a · √b = √(ab) only works when a and b are not both negative. So write each root with i first, then multiply.
Remember i · i = i² = −1.

questions.prompt: Simplify √(−4) · √(−9).
questions.hint: Convert each root to a multiple of i first.

questions.prompt: Simplify √(−4) · √(−25). Give a number.
Simplify (√(−3))².
Write 5 + √(−32) in the form a + bi.
In 7 − 3i, what number multiplies i? Give the number, including its sign.
Simplify i⁶ · √(−16).
questions.hint: i⁶ is i² after dividing 6 by 4. And √(−16) = 4i.

questions.prompt: Solve x² + 3 = −6. The solutions are ±bi. What is b?
Which expression is a real number?
questions.hint: Check what each one simplifies to.
questions.solution: i⁶ = −1 is real. i⁷ = −i, i⁹ = i and √(−7) = i√7 are imaginary.

teach.title: Adding and subtracting
text: A complex number is a + bi. Add or subtract the real parts together and the i parts together, like combining like terms.
When you subtract, distribute the minus sign to both parts of the second number.

questions.hint: Add the real parts. Add the i parts.
Real with real, imaginary with imaginary. Watch the signs.

questions.prompt: Subtract: (6 + 4i) − (2 + i)
questions.hint: Subtract the real parts and subtract the i parts.

questions.prompt: Subtract: (3 − 5i) − (−2 + 4i)
questions.hint: Distribute the minus sign to both parts of −2 + 4i.

questions.prompt: What is the real part of (9 + 2i) − (4 + 7i)?
questions.hint: Only subtract the real numbers: 9 and 4.
questions.solution: 9 − 4 = 5. The result is 5 − 5i, so the real part is 5.

questions.prompt: (2 + 5i) + (−2 − 3i) = bi. What is b?
questions.hint: The real parts cancel. Add the i parts.
questions.solution: 2 + (−2) = 0 and 5i − 3i = 2i. So the sum is 2i and b = 2.

questions.prompt: Add 4i to (−3 + 2i).
questions.hint: 4i is an imaginary term, so it joins the 2i.

questions.prompt: (4 + 3i) + (x + yi) = 10 − i. What is x?
questions.hint: Match the real parts on both sides.
questions.solution: Real parts: 4 + x = 10, so x = 6. (The i parts give 3 + y = −1, so y = −4.)

teach.title: Multiplying complex numbers
text: Multiply like binomials (FOIL). Then replace i² with −1 and combine.
A number times a + bi is distributed to both parts.

questions.prompt: Multiply: 2(3 + 4i)
Multiply: i(3 + 2i)
Multiply: (4i)(5i)
Multiply: (1 + 2i)(3 + i)
Multiply: (2 − i)(4 + 3i)
questions.hint: The last term is (−i)(3i) = −3i², which is +3.

questions.prompt: (3 + 2i)(3 − 2i) is a real number. What is it?
questions.hint: The i terms cancel. The last term is −4i² = +4.

questions.prompt: Multiply: (4 − 3i)²
questions.hint: Write (4 − 3i)(4 − 3i) and FOIL. Do not just square each term.

questions.prompt: (2 + 3i)(1 − i) = a + bi. What is a?

teach.title: Conjugates
text: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi. Only the sign of the i part changes.
A number times its conjugate is always real: (a + bi)(a − bi) = a² + b².

steps: This is a number times its conjugate.

teach.title: Dividing complex numbers
text: You cannot leave i in the denominator. Multiply the top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator.
The denominator becomes a real number, then split into a + bi form.

steps: Multiply top and bottom by 1 − i.

questions.prompt: What is the conjugate of 3 + 7i?
questions.hint: Change only the sign of the i part.

questions.prompt: What is the conjugate of −2 − 5i?
questions.hint: Keep the real part. Flip the sign of the i part.
A number times its conjugate is a² + b².

questions.prompt: Simplify 4 / (1 + i).
questions.hint: Multiply top and bottom by 1 − i.

questions.prompt: Simplify 10 / (3 − i).
questions.hint: The conjugate of 3 − i is 3 + i.

questions.prompt: Simplify (2 + i) / (1 − i).
questions.hint: Multiply top and bottom by 1 + i. Then divide both parts by the denominator.
questions.solution: Top: (2 + i)(1 + i) = 2 + 2i + i + i² = 1 + 3i. Bottom: 1 + 1 = 2. So the answer is 1/2 + (3/2)i.

questions.prompt: You multiply (3 + i)/(2 + i) top and bottom by 2 − i. What is the new denominator?
Simplify (3 + i) / (2 + i).
questions.hint: Multiply top and bottom by 2 − i.
questions.solution: Top: (3 + i)(2 − i) = 6 − 3i + 2i − i² = 7 − i. Bottom: 5. So the answer is 7/5 − (1/5)i.

teach.title: Putting it together
text: Work in steps: do powers and products first, then add and subtract, and divide last. Always finish in a + bi form.
Check: i² = −1 and 1/i = −i.

questions.prompt: Simplify (1 + i)².
Simplify (2 + 3i) + (1 − i)(2 + i).
Evaluate (2 + 3i)(2 − 3i) + i². Give a number.
questions.hint: The first product is a number times its conjugate.

questions.prompt: Evaluate x² − 2x + 2 when x = 1 + i. Give a number.
Simplify (3 + 2i) / i.
questions.hint: Multiply top and bottom by −i (the conjugate of i).

questions.prompt: If z = 2 + 5i, what is z times its conjugate?
Simplify (5 + 5i) / (1 + 2i).
(1 + 2i)(3 − i) = a + bi. What is b?

teach.title: The number that completes the square
text: x² + bx + c is a perfect square when c = (b/2)². Half of b, squared.
Then x² + bx + (b/2)² = (x + b/2)².

example.problem: Find c so that x² + 6x + c is a perfect square

questions.prompt: x² + 8x + c is a perfect square. What is c?
x² + 10x + c is a perfect square. What is c?
x² − 12x + c is a perfect square. What is c?
questions.hint: Half of −12 is −6. Squaring removes the sign.

questions.prompt: Which is the factored form of x² + 6x + 9?
Which is the factored form of x² − 14x + 49?
questions.hint: The middle term is negative, so the sign inside is negative.

questions.prompt: x² + 3x + c is a perfect square. What is c? Give a fraction or decimal.
x² − 5x + c is a perfect square. What is c? Give a fraction or decimal.
Which is a perfect square trinomial?
questions.hint: Check whether the last term is (half of 10) squared.
questions.solution: Half of 10 is 5 and 5² = 25. Only x² + 10x + 25 = (x + 5)² works.

teach.title: Solving by completing the square (a = 1)
text: 1) Move the constant to the right side. 2) Add (b/2)² to both sides. 3) Factor the left side as a square. 4) Take square roots, remembering ±. 5) Solve for x.

steps: Half of 6 is 3. 3² = 9. Add 9 to both sides: x² + 6x + 9 = 16.

questions.prompt: Solve by completing the square: x² + 4x = 5
Solve by completing the square: x² − 6x = 16
Solve: x² + 10x + 21 = 0
questions.hint: Move 21 to the right side first.

questions.prompt: Solve: x² − 2x − 15 = 0
questions.hint: Move 15 to the right. Then add (−2/2)² = 1.

questions.prompt: To complete the square for x² + 12x = 5, what number do you add to both sides?
Solve: x² − 8x + 7 = 0
Solve x² + 4x − 1 = 0 by completing the square.
Solve x² + 2x + 5 = 0 by completing the square.

teach.title: When a is not 1
text: Divide every term by a first so the x² coefficient is 1. Then complete the square as before.
You can also solve a fractional b, such as x² + 5x: half of 5 is 5/2.

questions.prompt: Solve: 2x² + 12x = 14
Solve: 3x² − 12x = 15
Solve: x² + 3x − 10 = 0
Solve: 2x² + 12x − 14 = 0
questions.hint: Move the 14 first, then divide by 2.
questions.solution: 2x² + 12x = 14, so x² + 6x = 7. This gives (x + 3)² = 16, x = 1 or x = −7.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in solving 4x² − 8x = 12 by completing the square?
choices: Take the square root of both sides
questions.hint: Get the coefficient of x² to be 1.

questions.prompt: Solve: 5x² + 20x = −15
Solve: 2x² − 12x + 10 = 0
Solve: x² + 5x + 4 = 0

teach.title: Rewriting in vertex form
text: Vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k. To get it, complete the square on the x terms. Whatever you add inside, subtract right away so nothing changes.
The vertex is (h, k).

example.problem: Write y = x² + 6x + 5 in vertex form

teach.title: Vertex form when a is not 1
text: Factor a out of the x terms first. Then complete the square inside. Remember what you add inside is multiplied by a.

steps: Factor 2 from the x terms: y = 2(x² + 4x) + 3.
Add 4 inside. That is really adding 2 · 4 = 8, so subtract 8: y = 2(x² + 4x + 4) − 8 + 3.

questions.prompt: Write y = x² + 4x + 1 in vertex form.
Write y = x² − 10x + 30 in vertex form.
y = x² + 8x + 20 in vertex form is y = (x + 4)² + k. What is k?
What is the vertex of y = x² − 6x + 2?
questions.hint: Complete the square, then read (h, k) from y = (x − h)² + k.

questions.prompt: Write y = 2x² + 12x + 7 in vertex form.
questions.hint: Factor 2 from the x terms. The 9 you add inside counts 2 · 9 = 18.

questions.prompt: Write y = −x² + 4x − 3 in vertex form.
questions.hint: Factor −1 from the x terms: −(x² − 4x). Then add 4 inside.

questions.prompt: y = x² − 4x + 9 in vertex form is y = (x − 2)² + k. What is k?
What is the vertex of y = 3x² − 12x + 5?
questions.hint: Factor 3 from the x terms, complete the square, and remember the 3.

teach.title: The discriminant
text: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is D = b² − 4ac. It tells you what kind of solutions to expect.
D > 0: two real solutions. D = 0: one real solution (repeated). D < 0: no real solutions, two complex solutions.

steps: D < 0, so there are two complex solutions.

questions.prompt: Find the discriminant of x² − 6x + 5.
questions.hint: a = 1, b = −6, c = 5. Square b first: (−6)² = 36.

questions.prompt: Find the discriminant of 2x² + 3x − 2.
Find the discriminant of x² + 4x + 4.
Find the discriminant of 3x² − 2x + 1.
Find the discriminant of x² + 3x − 10. What does it tell you?
questions.hint: D = 9 − 4(1)(−10). Is it positive, zero or negative?
questions.solution: D = 9 + 40 = 49 > 0, so there are two real solutions.

questions.prompt: The discriminant of a quadratic is 0. How many real solutions does it have?
questions.solution: If D = 0, then x = −b / 2a only. One real (repeated) solution.

questions.prompt: What type of solutions does x² + 2x + 7 = 0 have?
questions.solution: D = 4 − 28 = −24 < 0, so there are two complex (non-real) solutions.

questions.prompt: x² + kx + 9 = 0 has exactly one real solution, and k > 0. What is k?
questions.hint: One solution means D = 0. Write D = k² − 36.
questions.solution: k² − 36 = 0, so k² = 36 and k = 6 (since k > 0).

teach.title: Number and type of solutions
text: If D > 0 and D is a perfect square (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...), the two real solutions are rational. If D > 0 and not a perfect square, they are irrational.
For a parabola, D < 0 means it never crosses the x-axis. D = 0 means it touches the x-axis once.

example.problem: What type of solutions does x² − x − 1 = 0 have?
steps: 5 is not a perfect square, so they are irrational.

questions.prompt: What type of solutions does 5x² − x + 2 = 0 have?
What type of solutions does 4x² − 12x + 9 = 0 have?
What type of solutions does x² − x − 1 = 0 have?
questions.hint: D = 1 + 4. Is it a perfect square?
questions.solution: D = 5 > 0 but 5 is not a perfect square. So two real irrational solutions.

questions.prompt: What type of solutions does 6x² + x − 2 = 0 have?
questions.solution: D = 1 + 48 = 49 = 7². A positive perfect square, so two real rational solutions.

questions.prompt: x² + 5x + c = 0 has discriminant 9. What is c?
For which values of c does x² + 4x + c = 0 have two complex solutions?
questions.solution: 16 − 4c < 0, so 4c > 16 and c > 4. Dividing by a positive number does not flip the sign.

questions.prompt: How many real solutions does −2x² + 3x − 5 = 0 have?
Does the parabola y = x² − 4x + 7 cross the x-axis?
questions.hint: The x-intercepts are the solutions of x² − 4x + 7 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 16 − 28 = −12 < 0. No real solutions, so no x-intercepts.

teach.title: The quadratic formula
text: For ax² + bx + c = 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a).
Put the equation in standard form first so you read a, b, c correctly. The ± gives two answers.

Solve with the quadratic formula: x² − 7x + 10 = 0

teach.title: When the discriminant is negative
text: A negative D gives √(−D) = i√D. The solutions are complex, in the form a ± bi.
Simplify by dividing every part of the numerator by 2a.

questions.prompt: Solve x² + 2x + 5 = 0.
Solve x² − 4x + 13 = 0.
Solve x² + 6x + 10 = 0.
Solve 2x² − 4x + 5 = 0.

questions.hint: Read the part with no i.

questions.prompt: Solve: x² − 3x − 4 = 0
Which equation has a discriminant of −7?
questions.solution: x² + x + 2: 1 − 8 = −7. The others give 9, 1 and 0.

teach.title: The projectile model
text: An object thrown or dropped, with height in feet and time in seconds: h(t) = −16t² + vt + s.
v is the starting upward speed in ft/s (0 if dropped). s is the starting height in feet. At t = 0, h = s.

steps: s = 5, so it starts 5 ft above the ground.
v = 48, so it is thrown upward at 48 ft/s.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 32t + 6. How many feet above the ground does it start?
questions.solution: h(0) = 6, so it starts 6 ft up.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 60t + 2. What is the initial upward velocity in ft/s?
questions.hint: Look at the coefficient of t.
questions.solution: v is the coefficient of t, so v = 60 ft/s.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 40t + 3. Find h(1), the height in feet after 1 second.
A ball is thrown upward at 50 ft/s from a height of 8 ft. Which model fits?
questions.hint: v goes with t. The starting height is the constant. Gravity makes the t² term negative.
questions.solution: h(t) = −16t² + vt + s with v = 50 and s = 8.

questions.prompt: A rock is dropped from 100 ft, so h(t) = −16t² + 100. Find h(2).
A ball is dropped from the top of a 144-ft building. Which model fits?
questions.hint: Dropped means v = 0, so there is no t term.

questions.solution: h(3) = −144 + 144 + 10 = 10 ft. It is back at its starting height.

teach.title: Maximum height and time to the top
text: The graph is a parabola that opens down, so the vertex is the highest point.
Time to the top: t = −b/(2a). Max height: plug that t into h(t).

example.problem: Find the max height of h(t) = −16t² + 64t + 5

h(t) = −16t² + 32t + 4. What is the maximum height in feet?
questions.hint: Plug the time from the last question into h(t).

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 80t. At what time (in seconds) is the object highest?
h(t) = −16t² + 80t. What is the maximum height in feet?
h(t) = −16t² + 96t + 10. At what time (in seconds) is it highest?
h(t) = −16t² + 96t + 10. What is the maximum height in feet?
Which formula gives the time when h(t) = at² + bt + c is at its maximum?
questions.hint: This is the x-coordinate of the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex of a parabola is at t = −b / (2a).

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 16t + 3. What is the maximum height in feet?

teach.title: When does it hit the ground?
text: The ground is height 0. Set h(t) = 0 and solve. Factor or use the quadratic formula.
Time cannot be negative, so throw away any negative solution.

example.problem: When does h(t) = −16t² + 32t + 48 hit the ground?
steps: Negative time is not possible. It lands after 3 seconds.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 64t. At what time (in seconds, other than t = 0) is h = 0?
questions.solution: −16t(t − 4) = 0, so t = 0 or t = 4. It lands at t = 4 seconds.

questions.prompt: A rock is dropped from 144 ft: h(t) = −16t² + 144. How many seconds until it lands?
questions.hint: Set h = 0 and solve for t².

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 16t + 32. How many seconds until it lands?
questions.solution: (t − 2)(t + 1) = 0, so t = 2 or t = −1. Only t = 2 makes sense.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 48t + 160. How many seconds until it lands?
questions.solution: (t − 5)(t + 2) = 0, so t = 5 or t = −2. It lands at 5 seconds.

questions.prompt: When solving h(t) = 0 you get t = 4 and t = −1. Which do you keep, and why?
choices: t = 4, because time cannot be negative
Both, because a quadratic has two answers
t = 4, because it is the larger zero
questions.hint: Think about what t stands for.
questions.solution: t is time after launch, so it has to be 0 or more. Keep t = 4.

questions.prompt: h(t) = −16t² + 20t + 6. Use the formula to find the landing time in seconds.
A rock is dropped from 400 ft. How many seconds until it lands?
h(t) = −16t² + 8t + 3. When does it hit the ground?

teach.title: Area problems
text: Name the unknown side x. Write the other side in terms of x. Write area = length × width, set up the equation, and solve. Reject answers that are negative or make no sense.
For a fence problem, the perimeter or fence length gives a relationship between the sides.

example.problem: A rectangle is 3 ft longer than it is wide and has area 40 ft². Find the width.
steps: Let width = w, so length = w + 3. Then w(w + 3) = 40.

teach.title: Maximum area
text: If the area is a quadratic with a negative leading coefficient, its vertex gives the maximum area.

example.problem: 60 ft of fence makes 3 sides of a rectangle against a barn. What width x gives the most area?
steps: The two widths use 2x. The length is 60 − 2x.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 4 ft longer than it is wide, and its area is 60 ft². What is the width in feet?
The length of a garden is twice its width, and the area is 72 ft². What is the width in feet?
A rectangle has perimeter 36 ft and area 80 ft². How long is its shorter side in feet?
questions.hint: The sides add to 18. If one side is w, the other is 18 − w.
questions.solution: w(18 − w) = 80, so w² − 18w + 80 = 0. (w − 8)(w − 10) = 0. The sides are 8 and 10. The shorter is 8.

questions.prompt: 60 ft of fence makes 3 sides of a rectangle against a barn. The width is x, so A = x(60 − 2x). What x gives the most area?
For the fence above, what is the maximum area in ft²?
A ball is thrown from 24 ft at 40 ft/s: h(t) = −16t² + 40t + 24. What is its height after 2 seconds?
For h(t) = −16t² + 40t + 24, how many seconds until it hits the ground?
questions.solution: (2t + 1)(t − 3) = 0, so t = −1/2 or t = 3. Keep t = 3 seconds.

questions.prompt: For h(t) = −16t² + 40t + 24, what is the maximum height?
questions.hint: The top is at t = −40 / (−32) = 1.25 seconds.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = −2(x + 4)² + 9, and does it open up or down?
questions.hint: In y = a(x − h)² + k the vertex is (h, k). The sign of a decides the direction.
questions.solution: x + 4 = x − (−4), so h = −4. k = 9. a = −2 is negative, so it opens down.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = (x − 7)² − 11?
questions.hint: The minimum of a parabola that opens up is the k value of the vertex.
questions.solution: Vertex is (7, −11). a = 1 > 0, so the minimum value is −11.

questions.prompt: Find the axis of symmetry of y = 3x² − 18x + 4. Give the value of x.
What is the range of y = −x² + 6x − 5?
questions.hint: Find the vertex. The parabola opens down.
questions.solution: x = −6 / (−2) = 3. y = −9 + 18 − 5 = 4. It opens down, so the range is y ≤ 4.

questions.prompt: Factor 10x² − 9x − 9.
questions.hint: Try pairs for 6x² and for −3. Check the middle term by FOIL.

questions.prompt: Factor 49x² − 64.
questions.hint: This is a difference of squares: a² − b².

questions.prompt: Solve: x² − x = 42
